parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation or documented traveler-facing restriction, with discrimination on gender identity criminalised since 2005 and equality law covering services and health. Documented exposure is general reported hate-crime suspicions, rising and without a penal hate-crime category, rather than state targeting, detention, or facility exclusion. Entry, screening and facility rules are unsourced, so uncertainty prevents a higher score despite a well-documented tolerant institutional climate.

entry_documents.protection: Gender-identity discrimination is a criminal offence since 2005 and equality law covers goods and services; no border refusal is documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Not documented. Unknown border practice does not override the absence of a documented refusal regime.

federal_state_facilities.protection: Equality statute covers goods, services, education and health services; no facility ban is documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: No subnational variation is documented and none should be inferred.

care_services.exposure: Resident survey reporting over 40% unable to access needed care has no field period and is not counted as current visitor prevalence; visitor care denial is not documented.
care_services.protection: Equality protections were extended to health services in 2014.
care_services.interaction: Centralised resident minor-care units do not establish a visitor-care rule.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No criminalisation of trans people or consensual same-sex activity; same-sex activity legal since 1971.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Discrimination on sexual orientation criminalised in 1995 and on gender identity in 2005; gender identity and expression covered.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Resident legal gender recognition reform in 2023 is only a climate signal, not a visitor protection.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minor gender care is via two centralised units; 2020 recommendations for under-25s prioritised psychosocial therapy and restricted blockers/hormones case-by-case. No visitor-minor or guardian rule is documented.
minors_guardians.protection: Blockers remain available case-by-case and hormones may be considered for permanent identity with severe dysphoria.
minors_guardians.interaction: Resident clinical recommendations do not establish denial to a travelling minor or guardian.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Record 1,808 suspected hate crimes; sexual-orientation/gender-identity category rose 72 to 241 over six years and is 12% of motives. No trans-specific killing or violence rate is documented; older LGBT-wide figures are dated and not trans-specific.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Police record motive in reports, but the criminal code has no hate-crime offence, so incidents are suspicions not charges.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Rising reported suspicions indicate street friction, while absence of a charging category weakens formal recourse.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Entry, passport-marker handling, screening and gendered-facility access remain unsourced and unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Criminal discrimination offence and equality statute provide formal recourse; a conversion-practices case was prosecuted as assault.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Formal protections coexist with no documented visitor-specific remedy operation and rising suspicions.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar absence of criminalisation with explicit equality protection, but this dossier documents less operative visitor remedy, police training and oversight, and leaves entry and facilities unsourced, so it sits below 0.85.

Similar harassment possibility under a functioning equality framework. This case has no documented nightlife assault pattern or facility exclusion, but also no documented hate-crime charging, placing it near or slightly above this anchor.
Higher than 0.65-B because no documented visitor care refusal, detention threat, or repeated discriminatory service failure is shown; remedies are formal rather than demonstrably failed.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is permissive law plus tolerant social visibility, with no documented traveler-facing state exposure. The principal risk is non-state harassment reflected in rising police-recorded suspicions and weak charging recourse due to no hate-crime offence. Unsourced border, screening and facility questions, and undated care-access material, create uncertainty but are not documented exposures. The 2023 recognition reform, marriage and conversion-ban developments are resident or climate signals only.
